name: Temporal
summary: A durable workflow platform that records workflow event history, dispatches workflow and activity tasks, and replays deterministic workflow code to resume progress after failure.

features.name: Durable workflow event history
features.description: Temporal persists workflow state transitions as event history, allowing a workflow execution to resume from recorded events rather than relying on one continuously running process.
benefits: Makes progress recoverable across worker and service failures
Provides an inspectable history for workflow execution
costs: History size and transition rate constrain workflow shape
Persisted history introduces storage and serialization overhead

features.name: Workflow and activity task queues
features.description: Temporal workers poll task queues for workflow tasks and activity tasks, separating durable workflow coordination from execution of external or potentially non-deterministic work.
benefits: Decouples service-side orchestration from worker capacity
Allows different worker pools to own workflow and activity execution
costs: Queue routing and worker availability affect progress latency
Task delivery requires explicit timeout and retry behavior

features.name: Deterministic workflow replay
features.description: A worker re-executes workflow code during replay and checks generated commands against the existing event history, so workflow code must obey Temporal's deterministic execution constraints.
benefits: Restores workflow local state without serializing every in-memory value
Turns recorded events into a recovery protocol for workflow code
costs: Non-deterministic workflow changes can cause replay failures
Replay consumes worker CPU and may be expensive for long histories

features.name: Activity retry and timeout boundary
features.description: Activities represent external work whose execution is bounded by timeout and retry policies, while the workflow history records the resulting command and event transitions.
benefits: Makes transient failure handling declarative at the workflow boundary
Separates workflow progress from individual activity attempts
costs: Retries can duplicate external effects unless activities are idempotent
Timeout and retry settings determine recovery latency and load

mathematical_views.question: How does a sequence of workflow commands and recorded events define durable progress for one workflow execution?
assumptions: The event history is the authoritative execution record
Workflow code is deterministic for the modeled history
The view abstracts persistence implementation and service sharding

mathematical_views.question: How do task queues and worker polling mediate transitions between persisted workflow state and executable work?
assumptions: A task queue identifies a compatible worker pool
At-least-once concerns are represented by task retry and timeout transitions
Worker scheduling latency is not treated as workflow state

mathematical_views.question: Which workflow observations remain stable when deterministic replay reconstructs local state while activities perform external effects?
assumptions: Activity results are represented by history events
External activity effects are idempotent or otherwise compensated
The model does not claim replay makes external systems transactional

costs: History storage and transition limits shape workflow design
Queue backlog and worker matching affect latency

benefits: Recoverable workflow-local state without checkpointing arbitrary memory
costs: Code evolution must preserve replay compatibility

benefits: Structured recovery for transient external failures
costs: Retries increase delay and can repeat external effects
